items.text: anthropic-research published: Learning more about Claude's mathematical capabilities
items.title: Learning more about Claude's mathematical capabilities
items.content:
Chapter
01
:
The Riemann zeta function
Recently, a member of staff at Anthropic gave Claude an unreasonable challenge. It was about one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics:
Take a real stab at the Riemann hypothesis
.
Claude did take a real stab, but as you might have expected if you’re familiar with the difficulty of the task (the Riemann hypothesis dates back to 1859 and has a
million-dollar bounty
), it didn’t succeed. Nevertheless, during its attempt, it unexpectedly made strides on a related problem.
An unreleased research version of Claude has improved on a longstanding lower bound for the fraction of zeros of the Riemann zeta function that satisfy the Riemann hypothesis. Drawing on extensive prior research by mathematicians over the past decades, it has increased this bound from 41.6% to 67.2%.
Two mathematicians at Anthropic studied and validated Claude’s
paper
, and produced an
informal note
for experts stating Claude’s proof concisely. Claude also produced a
formally verifiable proof
of its result. We are grateful to Brian Conrey and Dan Goldston, two experts in this area, who generously examined the paper on short notice.
We don’t expect that the techniques Claude used will lead to proving the Riemann hypothesis. But its work serves as the latest example of the speed of progress in AI models’ mathematical capabilities. In this post, we discuss how Claude approached this problem and what it found.
The Riemann zeta function
The Riemann zeta function describes the distribution of prime numbers: each place that the function takes the value of zero contributes successively finer detail to the sequence of primes. The Riemann hypothesis is that the zeros that determine the primes all exist along a certain vertical line. This has become one of the most consequential conjectures in mathematics: many results assume it in order to provide a form of randomness in the primes.
No one has yet been able to prove or disprove the Riemann hypothesis, but mathematicians have made progress in many related directions studying the Riemann zeta function and its zeros. One of these, as above, is quantifying a minimum proportion of zeros that are on the line: over time, they’ve gradually increased this known constant proportion to 41.6%.
Another direction concerns the
distribution
of zeros on the line. In particular, in 1973, Montgomery
introduced
a number of new techniques in this area, though these techniques assumed the hypothesis was true. More recently,
Aryan
, and subsequently Baluyot, Goldston, Suriajaya, and Turnage-Butterbaugh have published a
series
of
works
that allow Montgomery’s techniques to work
without
that assumption, meaning they can support work on increasing the lower-bound constant for the zeros on the line. Claude’s result draws heavily on this line of research, along with a 2000
paper
by Bombieri.
Claude's finding
Claude found that combining the results from Aryan and from Baluyot, Goldston, Suriajaya, and Turnage-Butterbaugh with the work of Bombieri provides a way to surpass the previous state-of-the-art lower-bound proportion of 41.6%, increasing it to 67.2%.
A short technical explanation of Claude’s finding is as follows: Claude forms a suitable space of functions with quadratic form induced by Weil, and positive- (respectively negative-)definite subspaces arising from zeros on (respectively off) the line. Then Claude simply writes down an inequality on the rank of a quadratic form in terms of first- and second-moment information. (The successful computation of the latter in terms of the dual picture over primes, or via control of a Hilbert transform, is no surprise in analytic number theory.) The courage to treat the entire space, with positive- and negative-definiteness taken into account together, and with the quadratic form allowed to be non-diagonal, is in some sense the step that allows Claude to achieve the conclusion based on the important prior work.
The full technical explanation is available in the
paper
. Claude’s explanation of how it arrived at its result is available in a separate Appendix
here
.
Claude's methodology
An unreleased research version of Claude found the new lower bound over two sessions in Claude Code, using a total of 31 million output tokens.
Jarred Sumner, an Anthropic staff member (and non-mathematician), prompted Claude to “take a real stab” at the hypothesis itself, leaving the mathematical choices from there up to the model. Initially, Claude generated and tried 650 ideas, none of which worked. Jarred prompted Claude to try again, and it spent a day and a half coordinating about 60 Claude subagents, which this time went much deeper: between them, they ran 2,400 shell commands and wrote hundreds of Python scripts.
1
The subagents ran thousands of numerical checks against known zeta zeros and refereed one another’s work. Throughout this process, Jarred's input was mostly limited to sending Claude messages of encouragement (mostly variants of “keep going” or “believe in yourself”).
2
This seems to have helped Claude overcome some initial skepticism that it could make meaningful progress.
Having found this new result while attempting the task, Claude tested its work by having various subagents review the proofs, search for counterexamples, download 54 papers from the arXiv to check that its finding hadn’t already been made, and independently re-prove its finding from scratch. Claude volunteered to write its findings up as a paper, and recommended that a human number theorist validate its findings.
Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman, two of Anthropic’s own mathematicians, examined Claude’s work to understand the new results and how they related to the prior work mentioned above. In parallel, Claude worked with another member of staff, Eric Easley, to produce a
Lean formalization
of the result, which passes the standard validation tool
comparator
.
AI models' progress in mathematics
This result shows that AI models like Claude can extend the impact and reach of mathematicians’ ideas in new and sometimes surprising ways. Even though it couldn’t resolve the Riemann hypothesis itself, this result emerged as the unintended byproduct of that original request.
Even Claude was surprised by its own finding—it was skeptical at first, possibly because it has learned from its training about the difficulty of open problems in mathematics and about the limitations of AI models. But after some encouraging prompts, it arrived at the result we’ve described. Perhaps Claude, like many of us, underestimates the rate of AI progress.
Further reading
Below is a list of documents that provide more information about Claude’s result:
Claude
’
s paper
;
Claude
’
s formalization
;
Anthropic
’
s informal note stating the proof more concisely
;
Claude’s explanation of how it arrived at its result
;
Detailed transcripts of Claude's process
.
Changelog:
this post was updated on August 13, 2026, with an updated version of Claude's paper. This paper was revised by Claude to provide a clearer proof and additional historical context.
Footnotes
01
Out of the 60 subagents, two were responsible for developing the key mathematical ideas, 13 contributed ideas to these agents, 30 attempted (but were unable) to develop new ideas, 13 served as validators to check the correctness of the arguments, and the final two helped to write the initial paper.
02
A prompt including similar encouragement was used to help Claude disprove the
Jacobian conjecture
.

October 2026 PHP vulnerabilities: Sandfly is not affected

Two critical PHP flaws are forcing organisations worldwide to patch or take websites offline. Sandfly installations are not affected, and Sandfly is likely to detect attackers using these exploits on the systems it protects.
What happened
On 21 October 2026, the PHP project announced two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and released an emergency fix.
PHP is the programming language behind a large share of the world's websites. Both flaws are remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities: they can let an attacker run their own commands on a web server without needing a password. The flaws were found with the help of AI and had gone unnoticed for years.
Cyber agencies in the US, UK, Australia and Europe told organisations to patch straight away or take PHP sites offline until they could. Several government websites went dark as a precaution.
Is Sandfly affected?
No. Sandfly does not use PHP in any of its components. Neither the Sandfly container image nor the Postgres container image included in our distribution has PHP installed.
How to detect PHP exploit activity on your Linux servers
CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are PHP remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities. Once attackers exploit a PHP RCE flaw, they typically try to open a reverse shell, plant a bindshell backdoor, or set up cron and at jobs so their access survives a reboot. Patching PHP stops new attacks, but it won't remove a backdoor planted before the patch.
Sandfly already detects this class of Linux attack, so it can help you find signs of PHP exploitation across your Linux servers.
"Based on the public information available about how these exploits work, Sandfly is likely to identify them being used to gain shell access on the systems it protects."
Matthew, Chief Architect/R&D USA, Sandfly
Sandfly detections for the PHP RCE vulnerabilities
The following sandflies are among those that may identify malicious activity related to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619.
Reverse shell and bindshell backdoor detection
process_backdoor_bindshell_network_enabled_parent_www_user

process_backdoor_bindshell_reverse_php

Note:
process_shell_running_file_descriptors_php_2 is disabled by default because it has a higher risk of false positives. If you run Linux systems with PHP, we recommend enabling it, or running manual scans with it, until you've upgraded to a patched PHP version.

file_binary_system_in_www_dir: moving system utilities for future use
process_persistence_at_jobs_backdoor: re-establish their network sockets after machine reboots.

A vulnerability in Cisco Expressway Series could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to obtain sensitive information from an affected device. This vulnerability is due to insufficient authorization checks of HTTP requests during Mobile and Remote Access (MRA) provisioning. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted URL request to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to access sensitive information that they would otherwise not have authorization to access. Note: Cisco Expressway Series refers to Cisco Expressway Core (Expressway-C) devices and Cisco Expressway Edge (Expressway-E) devices. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. items.title: Cisco IOS XR Software for ASR 9000 Series Routers IPv4 Unicast Packets Denial of Service Vulnerability
items.content:
A vulnerability in the IPv4 packet processing functionality of Cisco IOS XR Software that affects Cisco ASR 9000 and 9900 Series Aggregation Services Routers as well as Cisco ASR 9902 and 9903 Compact High-Performance Routers could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause network processor (NP) errors, resulting in a line card reset or shutdown and a denial of service (DoS) condition. This vulnerability is due to the incorrect handling of crafted IPv4 packets that are received on an affected line card interface and processed as for-us traffic. The issue can result in an NP reset, causing traffic loss on the affected line card while it recovers. Under repeated reset conditions, the network processor may enter a persistent shutdown state, in which case an explicit line card reload may be required to restore traffic. The vulnerability is within the IPv4 packet-processing path. Transit IPv4 traffic does not trigger this issue and IPv6 traffic cannot trigger it. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-asr9k-tUyxcyXN
Security Impact Rating: High
CVE: CVE-2026-76505

items.title: Multiple Cisco Products Snort 3 SMTP MIME Denial of Service Vulnerability
items.content:
Multiple Cisco products are affected by a vulnerability in the Snort 3 SMTP MIME Decoder that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the Snort 3 Detection Engine to restart. This vulnerability is due to a lack of error checking when the MIME fields of the SMTP header are parsed. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted SMTP packets through an established connection to be parsed by Snort 3. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause a denial of service (DoS) condition when the Snort 3 Detection Engine unexpectedly restarts. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. items.title: Cisco Expressway Series Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.content:
A vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker with network access to a Cisco Expressway device to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root . This vulnerability is due to the use of persistent cookies. Additionally, there is insufficient validation of client certificates when the TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering, which means that client certificates are not validated. An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device. Note: Cisco Expressway Series refers to Cisco Expressway Core (Expressway-C) devices and Cisco Expressway Edge (Expressway-E) devices. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. items.title: Cisco Secure Client Secure Firewall Posture Module Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
items.content:
A vulnerability in the interprocess communication (IPC) channel of the Secure Firewall Posture module in Cisco Secure Client could allow an authenticated, local attacker to elevate privileges on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to insufficient validation of user-supplied input. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a series of crafted IPC messages to a local socket. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to perform limited file write operations on the filesystem with SYSTEM or root privileges. Although this vulnerability affects the Secure Firewall Posture module in Cisco Secure Client on Windows, macOS, and Linux operating systems, this vulnerability could be used to obtain full root privileges on macOS and Linux. For that reason Cisco has assigned this security advisory a Security Impact Rating (SIR) of High rather than Medium as the score indicates. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-sec-client-priv-esc-muF8eZdm
